name: Idiopathic/Heritable Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension

criteria.description: Mean pulmonary arterial pressure (mPAP) ≥ 25 mmHg at rest measured by right heart catheterization
Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure (PCWP) ≤ 15 mmHg to exclude left heart disease
Exclusion of other causes of pulmonary hypertension such as connective tissue disease, congenital heart disease, or chronic thromboembolic disease
Positive family history of pulmonary arterial hypertension or identification of pathogenic mutations in PAH-associated genes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated mean pulmonary arterial pressure ≥ 25 mmHg at rest with PCWP ≤ 15 mmHg and elevated PVR > 3 Wood units on right heart catheterization, after exclusion of secondary causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for BMPR2 and other mutations is recommended in suspected heritable cases.

searchTerms: heart or blood vessel function abnormality

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) or NT-proBNP levels indicating right ventricular strain
Normal or mildly elevated liver function tests secondary to hepatic congestion
imaging: Echocardiography showing right ventricular hypertrophy and dilatation
Right heart catheterization confirming elevated pulmonary arterial pressures and vascular resistance
Chest X-ray showing enlarged pulmonary arteries
genetic: Mutations in other genes such as ALK1, ENG, and SMAD9
other: 6-minute walk test showing reduced exercise capacity
Electrocardiogram with right axis deviation and right ventricular hypertrophy

distinguishingFeatures: History of pulmonary embolism or thrombosis
Imaging evidence of chronic thromboembolic obstruction
Elevated pulmonary capillary wedge pressure > 15 mmHg
Echocardiographic evidence of left ventricular dysfunction or valvular disease
Response to treatment of left heart disease

redFlags: Signs of right heart failure such as severe peripheral edema or ascites
Sudden onset chest pain with hemoptysis
references: Simonneau G, et al. Haemodynamic definitions and updated clinical classification of pulmonary hypertension. Eur Respir J. 2019.
Rich S, et al. Primary pulmonary hypertension: a national prospective study. Ann Intern Med. 1987.
